title: task complete rejects --final-summary and blames the actor for it
description:
`quest task complete <id> --final-summary "..."` is rejected, so writing a final summary at completion time requires two commands (`task edit --final-summary` then `task complete`). Reported by opum-marketplace while closing OMARK-42.

Verified 2026-09-11 against quest 0.6.0 in a scratch workspace:

  quest task complete T-1 --final-summary "done" --actor jdn --actor-kind human --json
  -> exit 2, {"error_type":"usage","message":"task complete requires a reference and an explicit actor."}

  quest task complete T-1 --actor jdn --actor-kind human --json
  -> exit 6, validation (an unrelated illegal-transition error) -- so the actor and reference parse fine

The diagnostic is the sharper half of this bug and was not in the original report. Both a reference and an explicit actor WERE supplied; the unknown flag is what failed. The message names two things the caller got right and says nothing about the one they got wrong, which sends them to re-check their actor declaration -- the most heavily ritualised part of a Quest write -- instead of to the flag. `quest help task complete` does list the accepted flags (--actor, --actor-kind, --accountable-human) and its usage line omits --final-summary, so the information exists; it is the error path that does not use it.

Two candidate fixes, not mutually exclusive, and choosing between them is this task's job:

A. Accept --final-summary on `task complete`. quest instructions task-finalization treats writing a final summary and moving to a terminal status as one step, so the two-command shape is a seam the workflow does not have. task complete already mutates the record; folding the summary in is not a new capability, and a single write also removes a window where a task is Done with no summary.

B. Make the usage error name the actual cause -- report the unrecognised flag, not a generic reference-and-actor sentence. This is worth doing even if A lands, because the same generic message will misdirect the next caller who mistypes any other flag. Check whether other commands share this message and misreport the same way; if so the fix belongs at the shared parser, not here.

Recommend both: A removes the two-command shape, B stops the parser lying about why a command failed.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A final summary can be written and the task moved to a terminal status without the caller needing two separate writes, OR the usage line and help output state plainly that --final-summary is not accepted on task complete and name the command that does accept it.
A quest task complete invocation carrying an unrecognised flag reports the unrecognised flag, and does not report a missing reference or actor when both were supplied.
Whether the misleading usage message is shared with other commands is established and stated; if it is shared, the fix lands at the shared parser rather than being patched per command.
A test covers the unrecognised-flag path asserting on the diagnostic content, not only on exit code 2 -- exit 2 was already correct here and is what made the wrong message survive.

plan: 1. Extend tasks.complete() in src/application/tasks/tasks.ts to accept an optional finalSummary and apply it to the task before transitioning
2. In src/cli/main.ts, allow --final-summary on the complete branch (~line 1990-2002) and wire it through
3. Fix the shared only() usage-error path (main.ts:339, 37 call sites) so a rejected flag is named in the message instead of the generic reference/actor sentence, without a per-command special case
4. Verify no other only() call site regresses by checking a representative sample (task edit, task create) still produce sensible messages
5. Add tests asserting on diagnostic content for the unrecognised-flag path on task complete
6. Record in implementation notes whether the fix is shared across commands (it is) and why it landed in the shared parser rather than per-command
7. bun run check must exit 0 before PR
implementationNotes: Second sighting of the same shared usage-error path (reported by opum-agent, 2026-09-12): `quest task edit <id> --implementation-notes "..."` also fails with no flag named -- `{"error_type":"usage","message":"task edit received invalid arguments."}`, exit 2. `--implementation-notes` is a real flag on `task create` but task edit has no such flag; its append-equivalent is `--add-note` (confirmed via `quest help task create` vs `quest help task edit`). This is the same shared usage-error path as the task-complete case already in this task's description, not command-specific: it strengthens AC #2/#3 (the message should name the unrecognised flag, and the fix likely belongs at the shared parser). The create/edit flag-name asymmetry is what makes the missing flag name expensive here: a caller who knows --implementation-notes from task create has no way to learn from the error that task edit spells it --add-note.

Direct literal reproduction (opum-agent, 2026-09-12), the exact case this task was filed for, not an analog:

  quest task complete OPAG-109 --final-summary "..." --actor opum-agent-orchestrator --actor-kind delegated-agent --accountable-human jdnewhouse
  -> {"error_type":"usage","message":"task complete requires a reference and an explicit actor.","principal":null}, exit 2

Reference and all three actor flags were present and correct; --final-summary is simply not a flag task complete accepts. Cost in practice: the caller read the message as an actor-declaration problem, checked their flags, found them correct, and only found the real cause by rerunning bare (the first run was piped, so the JSON error vanished and the write looked like a silent no-op). Worked around with task edit --final-summary then task complete (both exit 0, record ends Done with summary attached) -- useful as the fix's test shape.

Third confirmed sighting of the same shared usage-error path, after task edit --implementation-notes (see prior note). Reinforces AC #2/#3 further: task complete --final-summary, task edit --implementation-notes, and whatever else shares this path all misreport the same way.

Root cause (established before delegating to an implementer, recorded now so it survives a recycle): only(parsed, allowed) in src/cli/main.ts (~line 339) is a shared usage-error helper used at 37 call sites across the CLI dispatch. It returns a bare boolean and discards WHICH passed flag was outside the allowed set. The complete/archive/pause/start branch (~line 1990-2008) calls only(parsed, ["--actor","--actor-kind","--accountable-human"]) and on failure always emits the generic "task ${command} requires a reference and an explicit actor." -- so `task complete --final-summary ...` with a fully valid reference and actor still gets blamed on a missing actor, because --final-summary is simply not in the allowed set and the message never says so. This answers AC #2 directly: the misleading message IS shared across commands (task edit --implementation-notes hits the identical shape, already noted above), so the fix belongs at the shared parser (only() or a sibling helper that also reports the rejected flag(s)), not as a task-complete-only patch. The required fix has two parts, both recommended by this task's own description: (A) let task complete accept --final-summary, wiring it into tasks.complete() in src/application/tasks/tasks.ts (~line 635), which currently transitions the task with no way to set a final summary in the same write; (B) change the shared only()-based error path to name the actual rejected flag instead of the generic reference/actor sentence. Delegated to an opum-workflow:implementer in an isolated worktree (branch fix/QCLI-270-final-summary-and-flag-diagnostics) with this full brief; in progress as of this note.

Implemented on branch fix/QCLI-270-final-summary-and-flag-diagnostics, based fresh off origin/dev at fd3c24b. Part A: tasks.complete() in src/application/tasks/tasks.ts now takes an optional third finalSummary param, applied as a plain replace via taskState after transitionTask, matching task edit --final-summary semantics (not the clear/append vocabulary, which stays edit-only). src/cli/main.ts complete/archive/pause/start branch allows --final-summary only when command is complete; archive/pause/start keep the original actor-only allowlist. Additive: omitting the flag reproduces prior behavior exactly. Updated commandHelp and commandManifest task complete entries (fields: [finalSummary]) plus the golden copy in test/contract/command-contract.test.ts.

Part B (shared usage-error path, AC #2): confirmed the misleading message is shared, not task-complete-specific -- 37 call sites in src/cli/main.ts call only(parsed, allowed) and all discarded which flag(s) failed. Added unknownFlags(parsed, allowed) and a shared usageFailure(parsed, allowed, fallback) formatter next to only() around line 339; only() is now defined in terms of unknownFlags so behavior is unchanged for every existing caller. usageFailure names the offending flag(s) when unknownFlags is non-empty (Unrecognized flag --x. Accepted flags: ...), and falls back to the original sentence for every other rejection reason, so sites where the same guard also covers a missing positional argument (board export, task binding) keep their original correct message when the flags are actually fine.

Converted 21 of the 37 call sites that use the direct if (!parsed || !only(...)) return failure(usage, ...) idiom to usageFailure: init, instructions, agents, completion bash, sqlite-smoke, migration-smoke, manifest, board export, overview/board/doctor, cleanup, browser, search, task complete/archive/pause/start, task demote, task status-flow, task list, task view, task binding, task create, task edit-batch, task edit. Left unconverted: helps own inner --json/--plain check calls flags([]) on an always-empty array, so it can never observe an unrecognized flag -- structurally dead for this fix.

Explicit structural gap, stated rather than left silently inconsistent per this tasks own instruction: 15 call sites in the migration-backlog (preview/apply/status/rollback), milestone/decision (list/view/create/delete/edit/archive), and draft (list/view/create/promote/archive) action dispatchers use a positive-gate-per-action style: if (action equals x and only(parsed, allowed)) { ...; return ...; } cascading on failure to ONE shared bottom-of-group fallback message, e.g. milestone action is invalid or missing required arguments. By the time that fallback is reached, which actions allowlist was actually being evaluated is no longer known, so usageFailure cannot be dropped in without restructuring the whole if/else-if cascade per group -- a materially larger, riskier change than this tasks two named commands warrant. Left unconverted, documented here.

Verified end-to-end with the built CLI (bun src/cli/main.ts ..., not just unit tests) in a scratch git-init workspace. task complete <id> --final-summary ... --actor ... --actor-kind human --json exits 0, record ends status Done with finalSummary set, in one write (AC #0). Reproduced this tasks exact repro shape (reference plus --actor/--actor-kind delegated-agent/--accountable-human, plus a bogus flag) and got error_type usage, message Unrecognized flag --bogus-flag. Accepted flags: --final-summary, --actor, --actor-kind, --accountable-human, exit 2 -- names the flag, says nothing about a missing reference or actor (AC #1). task edit <id> --implementation-notes (the second-sighting repro) now names --implementation-notes and lists --add-note among the accepted flags. task archive <id> --final-summary no --actor ... --actor-kind human --json still correctly rejects --final-summary, confirming archive/pause/start are unchanged and complete-only is respected as designed.

Tests added/updated for AC #3 (diagnostic content, not just exit code). test/integration/tasks/cli-semantics.test.ts: updated the existing task create --bogus case to assert the full flag-naming message; added two new tests -- one proving task complete --final-summary completes and writes the summary in one command, one proving a real reference+actor with an added unrecognized flag on task complete reports that flag and does not contain the phrase requires a reference and an explicit actor. test/contract/cli-process.test.ts: updated the task edit --not-a-flag case to assert on message content instead of an exact match on the retired generic string. test/contract/command-contract.test.ts: updated the QCLI-147 source-scraping test to anchor on the new const editFlags array declaration instead of the now-absent inline only(parsed, [ call-site literal; added fields: [finalSummary] to the golden task complete manifest entry. bun run check (typecheck, lint, format:check, layer:check, full 468-test suite) exits 0 on this branch, fresh off origin/dev at fd3c24b.
finalSummary: Both fixes landed together as recommended. (A) task complete now accepts --final-summary and applies it as a plain replace in the same write as the terminal transition (src/application/tasks/tasks.ts). (B) The shared usage-error path (only() in src/cli/main.ts, used at 37 call sites) previously discarded which flag was rejected; added unknownFlags()/usageFailure() and converted the 21 call sites using the direct if-(!only)-return-failure idiom to name the actual unrecognized flag instead of a generic reference/actor sentence. The remaining 15 sites (migration backlog/milestone/decision/draft action dispatchers) use a positive-gate-per-action cascade to one shared fallback and cannot take this fix without a larger restructure -- documented in code and left as a known structural gap, not silently inconsistent. Verified with real command output: the exact repro (--final-summary plus a full delegated-agent actor plus a bogus flag) now returns "Unrecognized flag --bogus-flag. Accepted flags: ..." instead of blaming a missing reference/actor; task edit --implementation-notes now names the flag and lists --add-note. bun run check exits 0 (468/468 tests, including new coverage for both paths). Independently re-verified (full bun run check re-run, plus manual diff review of every changed file) by the orchestrating session before merge, not taken on the implementer's word alone.
